steps.title: Identify a problem
steps.description: Share everyday challenges and choose one to tackle as a team.

steps.title: Frame a question
steps.description: Turn the problem into a “How might we…?” question.

steps.title: Choose an idea
steps.description: Explore and compare ideas, then narrow them down to one.

items.title: Bring everyone together with a code
items.description: Send the code to teammates to join the same room.

items.title: Focus in timed steps
items.description: A timer for each step helps pace individual work.

items.title: Start privately
items.description: Your notes stay visible only to you until you share them.

items.title: Choose without seeing others' votes
items.description: Cast one favorite vote and three “likely needed” votes.

items.title: Find a new angle
items.description: Prompts help you see a problem from another perspective.

items.title: Take your outcome with you
items.description: Copy everything or save it as text for what comes next.

items.title: Gather
items.description: No one has to run the meeting. Once you join a room, the screen shows you what to do, one step at a time.

items.title: Write
items.description: Start on your own. Your notes stay visible only to you until you share them, so you can write down rough thoughts freely.
items.evidence: In spoken brainstorming, waiting to speak can reduce the number of ideas generated.

items.title: Share
items.description: Take turns talking through your notes. Ideas from people who find it hard to speak up get the same space.

items.title: Explore
items.description: Before jumping to ideas, turn a problem into a “How might we…?” question. When you get stuck, you get a new angle, not an answer.
items.evidence: Lack of market fit is one reason startups fail. Check the problem before the ideas.

items.title: Choose
items.description: Without seeing others' votes, place two kinds of stickers: a favorite (what you want to do) and “likely needed” (what others may need). Then talk through the votes and decide on one as a team.

items.title: Take it home
items.description: Copy the problem, question, and idea you chose, or save them as text.

background.heading: Where the approach comes from
background.description: Idea Boost draws on the Design Sprint, which Jake Knapp started at Google and GV developed into a method. Voting silently before discussing, and the two kinds of votes (favorite and “likely needed”), are also inspired by Design Sprint voting.
background.scope: Idea Boost helps you decide on one idea. Prototyping and user testing come next.
background.cases: Google's Design Sprint Kit includes case studies from 3M × Bontouch, H&M, and Headspace.
background.casesLabel: View Design Sprint Kit case studies

items.question: How long does it take?
items.answer: Teams that reached one idea took about two hours (median). Time varies with the number of people and the discussion. Each step has a timer to guide you.

items.question: Can I use it without knowing Design Sprints?
items.answer: Yes. A full Design Sprint takes five days, including prototyping and testing, with a facilitator leading the team. Idea Boost covers choosing one idea (usually the first three days) and guides you with step-by-step instructions and timers.

items.question: What do I need?
items.answer: A browser with an internet connection. You can start as a guest without a Google account by entering a name. This introduction page works on desktop and mobile. Full board functionality is not guaranteed on every smartphone.

items.question: How long are outcomes saved?
items.answer: People present at completion, and those who left after saving an outcome, can revisit it for 180 days after first completion. Incomplete shared outcomes are kept for 180 days after the last use. After that, they can no longer be viewed, so copy or save anything you want to keep. See “Storage and privacy” below.

items.question: Is this a Google product?
items.answer: No. Idea Boost is not a Google product and is not endorsed by or affiliated with Google. It draws on Design Sprint thinking.
